facts.name: Organizer problem and metric
facts.verified: Float32 single-band confidence raster; UTM11N; 100 m; [0,1]; 300 m triangular DTI, alpha .2 / beta .8
facts.limit: Local catalogue simulations do not reveal hidden test faults.

facts.name: Exact known-pixel masking
facts.verified: Staff: the mask is pixel-exact and identical to the provided training labels; a predicted pixel near a known trace but far from NEW truth is fully penalized (no buffer); a new-truth pixel CAN lie within 300 m of a known trace ('corrections or modifications to existing fault traces'); the same masking applies in the final re-evaluation.
facts.limit: Known pixels are neutral. Owner-reported scores corroborate this: 8GEMSDOE Hedge-v2 (all 60,988 catalogue pixels added as predictions) = GEMSDOE ens12 (0.1563 both).

facts.name: Hidden test-source disclosure
facts.verified: Fault types/source coverage are not disclosed; expert assessment matters.
facts.limit: Do not assume all test faults are quaternary scarps or geothermal conduits.

facts.name: Lopez-Paz & Oquab, ICLR 2017
facts.verified: Classifier trained separately from held-out two-sample evaluation; original statistic is accuracy.
facts.limit: Our AUC/refitted spatial adaptation assumes exchangeability; association is not causation.

facts.name: GeoDAWN official release
facts.verified: Summary text: the survey 'was divided into four separate acquisition blocks (from north to south: Winnemucca, Fallon, Hawthorne, and Tonopah; Figure 1)'; Area 1 and Area 2 are two overlapping survey specifications (Area 1 over Clayton Valley, inside the Tonopah block).
facts.limit: Block boundaries exist only as dashed lines in Figure 1; no coordinates are published. This repository's block raster is DERIVED from the figure (see audited derivation), not official coordinates.

facts.name: GeoDAWN contractor report
facts.verified: Winnemucca, Fallon, Hawthorne and Tonopah; two resolution/drape regimes; Tonopah helicopter acquisition. Figure 3 'The Four GeoDAWN Acquisition Blocks'; base stations (UTM): Winnemucca 432658E 4528343N, Fallon 349803E 4373452N, Hawthorne 357908E 4266948N, Tonopah 491299E 4213070N; tie lines extend >= 2 km into the adjacent block.
facts.limit: Figure 3 names the blocks, but official numeric boundaries are not published; base stations are not boundaries; tie lines overlap >= 2 km so membership near a seam is ambiguous. This repository's block raster is derived and audited, not official.

facts.name: Prize rules: submissions, selection, AI disclosure
facts.verified: Section 3.2: up to three submissions per week; generative-AI use allowed but must be disclosed in the narrative. Section 3.4: one final submission per entity, chosen without knowing private scores. Prize pool: Phase 1 $50,000 (top five $10,000 each), Phase 2 $250,000 ($100k/$70k/$40k/$25k/$15k).
facts.limit: Another account or repository is not a quota reset; confirm account compliance with the organizers.

facts.name: Competition end date vs rules deadline
facts.verified: Competition page: 'Dec. 3, 2026, 11:59 p.m. UTC'. Rules A.1: 'by 5:00 p.m. ET on the prize submission deadline date'.
facts.limit: Different time conventions on the same date; organizer confirmation needed (gemsprize@nlr.gov per the competition page).

facts.name: Pooled score, hand labels, new-fault definition
facts.verified: Public and private scores pool all pixels in the subset into ONE Tversky index; the final re-evaluation uses the entire GeoDAWN area. 'New fault' = any fault pixel not already captured by USGS/INGENIOUS, incl. newly mapped geometry of an existing system (thread 11536). Hand-labelling is permitted if labels are saved and available on request (thread 11543).
facts.limit: Chunking/subset sizes are not disclosed, so the public-subset truth density is inferred, not known.

facts.name: Qfaults positional accuracy (Hermant et al. 2025)
facts.kind: Peer-reviewed workshop paper cited on the organizers' About page
facts.verified: Figure 2 caption: in north-central Nevada the distance between USGS Quaternary faults and the authors' expert/lidar fault labels 'can be up to 400 m'; USGS mapping is 'occasionally imprecise at small scale'.
facts.limit: One study area. It supports 'corrections within a few hundred metres exist'; it does not give their prevalence in the hidden set.

facts.name: INGENIOUS Qfaults map-scale attribute
facts.kind: Owner CI receipt derived from GDR submission 1391
facts.verified: data/external/gdr_qfaults_traces.csv: 1,126 in-footprint traces, 1:100,000 (18.1% of length) and 1:250,000 (81.9%). Nominal 0.5 mm map accuracy is 50 m and 125 m respectively.
facts.limit: Per-pixel map-scale raster is not yet built, so the correction-corridor hypothesis that would use it is unvalidated. The NSHM23 fault-section database (1,017 simplified Quaternary-active sections compiled from the USGS Quaternary Fault Database) and NBMG's free 1:500,000 geologic-map fault data were read at description level only; neither is a new expert-mapped fault layer, so neither was pursued.
